skill.description: Anthony Fu's opinionated tooling and conventions for JavaScript/TypeScript projects. Use when setting up new projects, configuring ESLint/Prettier alternatives, monorepos, library publishing, or when the user mentions Anthony Fu's preferences.
skill.summary: Apply Anthony Fu's conventions to JavaScript and TypeScript projects.
skill.author: antfu

security_audit.summary: Forty-five static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown, fixed paths, or standard configuration examples. Ten alerts confirm package-manager, script, lint-fix, and hook execution guidance. No prompt injection or secret access was found; mutable third-party Actions create a high-severity supply-chain risk.

remediation.issue: Reusable GitHub Actions reference a mutable main branch, including a release workflow with write and OIDC permissions.
remediation.suggestion: Pin each reusable workflow to a reviewed commit SHA and keep every job permission at the minimum required level.

remediation.issue: Package-manager and project-script commands can execute downloaded code, lifecycle hooks, or repository-controlled scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation, show the exact command and working directory, and review package identities before execution.

remediation.issue: Lint fixes and installed Git hooks can modify repository files or run commands during local workflows.
remediation.suggestion: Check the working tree first, request confirmation, and summarize changed files after execution.

content.value_statement: JavaScript and TypeScript projects often accumulate inconsistent tooling and structure. This skill applies Anthony Fu's conventions for linting, testing, applications, libraries, and monorepos.
actual_capabilities: Applies TypeScript file organization, explicit import, comment, and testing conventions.
Configures @antfu/eslint-config for TypeScript, Vue, React, Next.js, Svelte, Astro, Solid, and UnoCSS.
Sets up Vue and Nuxt projects with explicit imports, UnoCSS, VueUse, and Storybook guidance.
Creates pnpm monorepo structures with recursive scripts, named catalogs, centralized aliases, and optional Turborepo guidance.
Prepares pure ESM TypeScript libraries with tsdown, generated declarations, exports, and API snapshots.
Provides .gitignore, GitHub Actions, VS Code, TypeScript, and Git hook configuration examples.
limitations: Recommendations are opinionated and may conflict with established project standards.
Examples assume JavaScript or TypeScript tooling, especially pnpm, Vitest, ESLint, Vue, Nuxt, and tsdown.
The skill provides guidance and examples; active agent permissions determine whether changes or commands can run.
Reusable GitHub Actions examples track a mutable main branch and require security review before adoption.

use_cases.title: Standardize a TypeScript Project
use_cases.description: Apply consistent file organization, imports, linting, formatting, tests, and package scripts to an existing codebase.

use_cases.title: Build a Vue Application
use_cases.description: Choose Vite or Nuxt, configure explicit imports, and establish Vue component and Storybook conventions.

use_cases.title: Publish a TypeScript Library
use_cases.description: Configure pure ESM builds, package exports, declaration files, API snapshots, and release preparation.

prompt_templates.title: Review Project Conventions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript project against Anthony Fu's conventions. List mismatches, prioritize low-risk changes, and do not edit files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner audit of an existing project

prompt_templates.title: Configure ESLint
prompt_templates.prompt: Configure @antfu/eslint-config for this Vue and TypeScript project. Preserve existing scripts and explain every required dependency.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Monorepo
prompt_templates.prompt: Set up a pnpm workspace with package scripts, named catalogs, and centralized aliases. Adapt every package name to this repository.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Library Publishing
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare this TypeScript monorepo for pure ESM publishing with tsdown, API snapshots, stale-build checks, CI, and minimal release permissions.

output_examples.input: Review my existing TypeScript project and identify convention gaps.
output: A prioritized review covering file structure, imports, comments, tests, linting, and package scripts.
Each recommendation distinguishes required corrections from optional opinionated changes.
Existing project conventions remain unchanged until the user approves edits.

output_examples.input: Prepare my Vue package for pure ESM publishing.
output_examples.output: A migration plan covering tsdown, declarations, package exports, API snapshots, build freshness checks, tests, and release safeguards.

best_practices: Review existing project conventions before applying opinionated defaults.
Pin third-party automation to reviewed commit hashes and grant minimal permissions.
Run focused tests and lint checks after changing configuration or package scripts.
anti_patterns: Do not replace established project conventions without explicit user approval.
Do not execute package binaries or release commands without reviewing package identity and repository state.
Do not copy mutable third-party workflow references into repositories with write permissions.

faq.question: Does this skill install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: No. It recommends commands and packages, while the active agent and user permissions control execution.

faq.question: Can it adapt an existing project?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare current conventions with the documented preferences and propose scoped changes.

faq.question: Does @antfu/eslint-config require Prettier?
faq.answer: No for supported source files. Optional formatter integrations may use Prettier for CSS, HTML, or Markdown.

faq.question: Which application frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The guidance covers Vue, Nuxt, Vite, UnoCSS, VueUse, and Storybook, with ESLint options for additional frameworks.

faq.question: Can this skill publish packages?
faq.answer: It can prepare publishing configuration and workflows. Publishing still requires user approval, valid credentials, and repository permissions.

faq.question: Are all recommendations mandatory?
faq.answer: No. Existing project standards take priority, and each recommendation should be adapted to the repository.
